# Going halves on a dumper

Lee,

Before we spend another year paying to use someone else’s dumper, I reckon this one in Faversham is worth a look. It’s a 2019 500kg tracked dumper, up for **£1,650 ono**. The bloke says it had new tracks last spring. Obviously we need to check it over, but at the asking price that’s **£825 each**, and we might get a bit off.

## The sums

We hired the tracked dumper from Sittingbourne for 14 days this year:

- **14 days at £85 = £1,190**
- **£30 delivery each time**, bringing what we spent to roughly **£1,600 all in**
- Buying this one outright: **£1,650 between us**

At this year’s use, the purchase price is covered by roughly a year’s saved hire bills. At half that use, it’s about two years. That’s **before servicing and repairs**, so I’m not pretending it’ll cost nothing to run.

We’ve already got three patio digs and the Boughton drive booked for spring, so there’s work waiting for it.

## It’s not just the hire bill

When they didn’t have one in September, we barrowed six tonnes of muck at Hernhill. That cost us two extra days, and your back was gone for a week. Then there was the delivery that turned up at 11, with half the morning wasted.

Having our own means it’s there when we need it, rather than hoping the hire place has one available and gets it to us on time.

## How we’d split it

We’d own it half each and keep it under cover in my lean-to at the yard. Routine servicing and normal wear-and-tear repairs would be 50/50, with any bigger expense agreed first. Fuel goes against whichever job it’s used on. If one of us breaks it through misuse, that person pays — different from something simply wearing out.

If it doesn’t work out, we can sell it and split the money. They seem to hold their value reasonably well, though there’s no guarantee we’d get everything back.

We’ve known each other 15 years, so we ought to be able to make this work. **Come and look at it with me this Saturday**, before someone else has it. No commitment until we’ve seen it running.
